objective: Use only existing source and WP-G3-CORR-015 evidence to separate physical contact chronology, collision-geometry identity, safety classification, and sampling latency; rank next-step design options without changing or executing the system.

user_authorization.source: user adoption of the proposed WP-G3-CORR-016 authorization through a response annotation
allowed: read-only analysis of existing local source and WP-G3-CORR-015 evidence

authoritative_inputs.role: scripted release, safety sampling, and target-pair chronology
release duration, settle count, sampling cadence, and physics dt
rim-support geometry history and evidence boundary

required_checks: target contact lies on or within the transformed overlay bounds
pre-release source-mesh contact is recorded separately
collider identity handoff is not mislabeled as proven loss and recreation of physical contact

matrix_dimensions: place or release versus retreat versus stage-free
source mesh versus competition rim-support primitive
safety_semantics.required_result: Record identical-pair accept/reject behavior for both classifiers and flag any divergence without choosing a repair.

required_checks: separate cached observation time from safety-emission time
identify the first scheduled scripted safety sample after release completion
do not infer physical onset from the failure marker alone

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Robot-to-bowl2 physical contact is already present before release through a source-mesh collider; release changes the active collider identity to the rim-support overlay.
predeclared_hypotheses.falsifier: No pre-release robot-to-bowl2 pair or geometry-inconsistent post-release target contact.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: The exact target pair is created by retreat motion.
predeclared_hypotheses.falsifier: The exact target pair is present in the cache-identical pre_retreat snapshot.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: The retreat-step-2 failure marker is delayed classification of a pre-existing pair under stage-dependent scripted safety semantics and five-step sampling.
predeclared_hypotheses.falsifier: The scripted predicate applies the same classification in release and retreat or the target is absent before retreat.

predeclared_hypotheses.statement: Scripted-expert and learned-policy G3 robot-bowl safety classifiers are semantically equivalent for the target pair.
predeclared_hypotheses.falsifier: One classifier rejects while the other accepts the identical target pair under an admissible equivalent state.

candidate_ranking_rules: Prefer a shared explicit collision-semantics contract and parity tests before runtime changes.
Do not rank a controller trajectory change above a semantics-contract defect unless the physical defect is independently established.
Treat safety-predicate relaxation or broadening as high-risk until the intended collision policy is explicit.
Treat rim-support geometry changes as task and asset changes requiring a new authorization and dynamic validation.
Treat another simulator run as lower priority than extracting all determinate conclusions from current evidence.

acceptance_matrix.expected: No simulator, remote, production source, controller, safety rule, asset, data, or training file is changed or executed.
Any robot-bowl2 contact and the exact target-pair chronology are reported separately.
The transformed target contact is consistent with the v4 rim-support box and all derived metrics are reproducible from the trace.
A static matrix proves equivalence or divergence from exact source semantics.
Observation and failure-emission clocks are separated exactly.
Focused review tests pass; all functional regressions pass; only the two immutable predecessor source-pin sentinels fail as expected.
A fresh no-overwrite terminal receipt and SHA-256 manifest verify.

claim_boundary: This local read-only design review may establish source semantics, derived geometry, chronology, evidence gaps, and ranked next-step options. It cannot establish the exact unobserved release step, counterfactual physical causality, correct safety policy, repair validity, generality, dataset readiness, G3 passage, AMD/ROCm behavior, hardware safety, or publication readiness.
